questions.question: Select the option that correctly expresses the given sentence in passive voice. I will never overlook this creativity.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that correctly expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
I will never overlook this creativity.

options.text: This creativity will never be overlooked by me.
options.html: This creativity will never be overlooked by me.

options.text: This creativity will be overlooked by me.
options.html: This creativity will be overlooked by me.

options.text: This creativity will being overlooked by me.
options.html: This creativity will being overlooked by me.

options.text: This creativity will not never be overlooked by me.
options.html: This creativity will not never be overlooked by me.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the active voice, the sentence is: "I will never overlook this creativity."
  • To convert to passive voice: Place the object "this creativity" at the beginning.
  • Change the active verb form "will never overlook" to "will never be overlooked" (future simple passive).
  • Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "me."
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Correct Sentence: "This creativity will never be overlooked by me."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 2: "This creativity will be overlooked by me." – Incorrect because it omits the word "never", changing the meaning.
  • Option 3: "This creativity will being overlooked by me." – Incorrect grammar (incorrect verb form).
  • Option 4: "This creativity will not never be overlooked by me." – Incorrect due to the double negative.

questions.question: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A place where birds are kept
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
A place where birds are kept
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 2'.

Key Points

  • Aviary refers to a place where birds are kept. It is often a large cage, building, or enclosure for keeping birds confined, especially for scientific study or display.

Hence, the correct answer is 'Option 2'.

Additional Information

  • Zoo is a place where animals, not specifically birds, are kept for public viewing.
  • Sanctuary refers to a protected area for wildlife but does not specifically mean a place for keeping birds.
  • Hive is related to bees, not birds.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Catastrophe
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Catastrophe
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Success.

Key Points

  • The word "Catastrophe" means a sudden and widespread disaster or a momentous tragic event. (महाविपत्ति)
    • Example: The earthquake was a catastrophe that destroyed many homes and lives.
  • "Success" refers to the accomplishment of an aim or purpose, or the attainment of fame, wealth, or social status. (सफलता)
    • Example: After years of hard work, she finally achieved great success in her career.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Success.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Nurture (पालन ​​पोषण): To look after and protect somebody/something while he/she/it are growing and developing.
    • Example: The beauty of nature is unparalleled.
  • Immaculate (निर्मल ): Perfectly clean, neat, or tidy.
    • Example: She always kept her room in immaculate condition.
  • Disaster (आपदा): A sudden event, such as an accident or a natural catastrophe, that causes great damage or loss of life.
    • Example: The flood was a major disaster that affected the entire region.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. After years of fights with his neighbour Ram, Shekhar decided to hold out the ______ and invited Ram for tea.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. One must be very strong to lift this box of glass jars.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
One must be very strong to lift this box of glass jars.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Weak.

Key Points

  • The word "strong" means having the power to move heavy weights or perform other physically demanding tasks. (मजबूत)
    • Example: He is strong enough to carry the heavy furniture by himself.
  • "Weak" refers to lacking physical strength and energy. (कमज़ोर)
    • Example: After the illness, he felt too weak to get out of bed.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'strong' is 'weak'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Weak.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Mighty (शक्तिशाली): Possessing great and impressive power or strength.
    • Example: The mighty warrior defended the kingdom bravely.
  • Complicated (जटिल): Involving many different and confusing aspects or elements.
    • Example: The instructions for the new software were very complicated.
  • Rugged (कठोर): Having a rough, uneven surface; not smooth or level.
    • Example: The rugged terrain made the hike more challenging.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. Anand personally believes in the motto, "When life gives you lemons, make lemonade."

Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

Anand personally believes in the motto, "When life gives you lemons, make lemonade."

options.text: Earn the maximum out of business
options.html: Earn the maximum out of business

options.text: Enjoy the most when the season is favourable
options.html: Enjoy the most when the season is favourable

options.text: Make the best out of difficult situations
options.html: Make the best out of difficult situations

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Make the best out of difficult situations.

Key Points

  • The idiom "When life gives you lemons, make lemonade" means making the best out of difficult situations. (कठिन परिस्थितियों का सर्वश्रेष्ठ बनाना)
    • Example: Despite the setbacks, she always manages to turn things around. Truly, when life gives her lemons, she makes lemonade.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Make the best out of difficult situations.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Earn the maximum out of business (व्यापार से अधिकतम कमाई करना): To make the highest possible profit from business.
    • Example: His goal was to earn the maximum out of business, always looking for new opportunities.
  • Nourish health (स्वास्थ्य को पोषित करना): To take care of and improve one's health.
    • Example: Regular exercise and a balanced diet help to nourish health.
  • Enjoy the most when the season is favourable (जब मौसम अनुकूल हो तो सबसे अधिक आनंद लें): To take full advantage of good times.
    • Example: They decided to enjoy the most when the season is favourable, planning picnics and outdoor activities.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Monotonous
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Monotonous
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Engrossing.

Key Points

  • The word "Monotonous" means something that is dull, tedious, and repetitious; lacking in variety and interest. (नीरस)
    • Example: The monotonous routine of his job made him feel unmotivated.
  • "Engrossing" refers to something that is absorbing all the attention or interest of someone; very interesting. (रोमांचक)
    • Example: The novel was so engrossing that she couldn't put it down until she finished it.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'Monotonous' is 'Engrossing'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Engrossing.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Tiresome (थकाऊ): Causing one to feel bored or annoyed.
    • Example: The long, tiresome journey left everyone exhausted.
  • Tedious (उबाऊ): Too long, slow, or dull; tiresome or monotonous.
    • Example: The tedious process of filling out forms made everyone impatient.
  • Rational (तार्किक): Based on or in accordance with reason or logic.
    • Example: His rational explanation convinced everyone in the meeting.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym to replace the underlined word in the given sentence. How did we end up in this rapturous situation?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym to replace the underlined word in the given sentence.
How did we end up in this rapturous  situation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ecstatic.

Key Points

  • The word "rapturous" means feeling or expressing great pleasure or enthusiasm. (उल्लासपूर्ण)

  • "Ecstatic" refers to feeling or expressing overwhelming happiness or joyful excitement. (परमानंदित)
    • Example: She was ecstatic when she heard the news of her promotion.
  • Hence, we can infer that "ecstatic" is a suitable synonym for "rapturous".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ecstatic.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Terrifying (डरावना): Causing extreme fear.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The mother asked the child, "Will you tell me who did accompany you to the airport?"
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. who accompanied you.

Key Points

  • The phrase "who accompanied you" is in the correct tense and form for the question being asked. (जो आपके साथ आया था)
    • Example: Can you tell me who accompanied you to the party?
  • "Will you tell me who did accompany you" is incorrect because "did" is redundant here and makes the sentence grammatically incorrect. (क्या आप मुझे बताएंगे कि आपके साथ कौन आया था)
    • Example:

​                  Incorrect: Will you tell me who did accompany you?

                  Correct: Will you tell me who accompanied you?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 1: who accompanies you (जो आपके साथ आता है): Present tense, not suitable for past events.
    • Example: She always accompanies you to the market.
  • Option 2: who does accompany you (जो आपके साथ आता है): Incorrect tense and redundant use of "does".
    • Example: Incorrect: Who does accompany you to school? Correct: Who accompanies you to school?
  • Option 4: who must be accompanied you (जो आपके साथ होना चाहिए था): Grammatically incorrect structure.
    • Example: Incorrect: Who must be accompanied you? Correct: Who must have accompanied you?

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the sentences in the correct sequence to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A) This past summer, my dream finally came true. B) Strange lands, exciting places, and new cultures have always fascinated me. C) Ever since I was a little girl, I dreamed about travelling overseas. D) I got to travel to England, France, Switzerland, and Germany.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the sentences in the correct sequence to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A) This past summer, my dream finally came true.
B) Strange lands, exciting places, and new cultures have always fascinated me.
C) Ever since I was a little girl, I dreamed about travelling overseas.
D) I got to travel to England, France, Switzerland, and Germany.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
Key Points
  • The paragraph begins by introducing the fascination with travel and dreams from a young age.
  • Sentence C is the first sentence as it sets the context of the lifelong dream:
    • "Ever since I was a little girl, I dreamed about travelling overseas."
  • Sentence B follows as it elaborates on the fascination with travel:
    • "Strange lands, exciting places, and new cultures have always fascinated me."
  • Sentence A is the third sentence because it describes the realization of the dream:
    • "This past summer, my dream finally came true."
  • Sentence D is the fourth as it provides specifics about the travel experience:
    • "I got to travel to England, France, Switzerland, and Germany."

The correct sequence is CBAD.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Rectify
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Rectify
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. amend.

Key Points

  • The word "rectify" means to correct something or make it right. (सही करना)
    • Example: She tried to rectify her mistake by apologizing to everyone involved.
  • "Amend" refers to making changes to something in order to improve it or correct it. (संशोधित करना)
    • Example: The government decided to amend the existing law to better protect the environment.
  • Hence, we can infer that the synonym of 'rectify' is 'amend'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. amend.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Mar (बिगाड़ना): To spoil, impair, or damage something.
    • Example: The graffiti marred the beauty of the historic building.
  • Corrupt (भ्रष्ट): Having or showing a willingness to act dishonestly in return for money or personal gain.
    • Example: The corrupt official was eventually caught and prosecuted.
  • Upset (परेशान): To make someone unhappy, disappointed, or worried.
    • Example: The news of her friend's accident upset her greatly.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. To _______ the ticket, Amith had to visit the travel agency many times.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

To _______ the ticket, Amith had to visit the travel agency many times.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'confirm'.
 
Key Points
  • The word "confirm" means to establish the truth or correctness of something. (पुष्टि करना)
  • In the context of the sentence, Amit had to visit the travel agency many times to verify or establish the validity of the ticket.

​Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 2'.

Complete Sentence: To confirm the ticket, Amith had to visit the travel agency many times.

Additional Information

The correct answer is Option 2.

questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Mobile phones or smartphones are becoming popular all over the world.

B. But at the same time, it also harms us in many ways.

C. It is the most widely used means of communication today.

    • "Mobile phones or smartphones are becoming popular all over the world."
  • Sentence C follows as it explains why they are so popular:
    • "It is the most widely used means of communication today."
  • Sentence D is the third sentence because it highlights their affordability and accessibility:
    • "Today, it is very affordable and available to everyone."
  • Sentence B is the fourth as it addresses the negative aspects:
    • "But at the same time, it also harms us in many ways."
  • The correct sequence is ACDB.

questions.question: Select the option that correctly expresses the following sentence in passive voice. Who invited you to this party?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that correctly expresses the following sentence in passive voice.
Who invited you to this party?

options.text: By whom you are invited to this party?
options.html: By whom you are invited to this party?

options.text: By whom are you invited to this party?
options.html: By whom are you invited to this party?

options.text: By whom you were invited to this party?
options.html: By whom you were invited to this party?

options.text: By whom were you invited to this party?
options.html: By whom were you invited to this party?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the active voice, the sentence is: "Who invited you to this party?"
  • To convert to passive voice: Place the object "you" at the beginning.
  • Change the active verb form "invited" to "were invited" (past simple passive).
  • Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "who".
  • Ensure the question structure remains intact by placing "By whom" at the beginning.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
Correct Sentence: "By whom were you invited to this party?"
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "By whom you are invited to this party?" – Incorrect word order in the question.
  • Option 2: "By whom are you invited to this party?" – Incorrect tense (present simple passive instead of past simple passive).
  • Option 3: "By whom you were invited to this party?" – Incorrect word order in the question.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error in the usage of the interjection. He replied / in a dry tone, / “Ouch! I will not work / for you anymore.”

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • The blank in the sentence refers to "Gandhi, (1) _______ father of the Indian nation."
  • The definite article "the" is the most appropriate choice because it specifies Gandhi's unique and universally recognized role as the father of the Indian nation.
  • Using "the" highlights the singular and significant status of Gandhi in this context.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "Gandhi, the father of the Indian nation, practiced ‘ahimsa’ in his personal and political life."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "an" – Incorrect, as "an" is used before words starting with a vowel sound, but it does not fit the context of specifying Gandhi's role.
  • Option 2: "for" – Incorrect, as "for" does not grammatically or contextually fit the blank.
  • Option 4: "a" – Incorrect, as "a" is indefinite and does not properly indicate Gandhi's specific and known title.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • The phrase "forest-living" refers to the place where animals live, which makes "Forest-living" the most appropriate choice in this context.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
 
Correct Sentence: "If violence is the law of the Forest-living-beasts, non-violence is the law of the civilised human species."
 
Additional Information
  • B: "life" – Incorrect because it doesn't carry a suitable meaning in this context.
  • C: "forest-live" – Incorrect choice for this sentence, as it doesn't fit the intended meaning.
  • D: "alive" – Refers more to the state of being, not the law of nature or survival.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • The blank refers to a general law applicable to all, not a specific individual. Hence, "one’s" is the most suitable choice to indicate a universal context.
  • Using "one’s" emphasizes the contrast between the laws governing animals and humans while maintaining grammatical correctness.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: “If violence is the law of the one’s beasts, non-violence is the law of the civilised human species.”
 
Additional Information
  • A: "her" – This option is incorrect as it implies a specific female subject, which is not contextually appropriate.
  • B: "its" – This option is incorrect as it would refer to animals or objects, but the context addresses a universal principle.
  • D: "one" – While grammatically valid, it lacks the possessive nuance required in the context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • The word "proven" is the past participle form that is appropriate for describing a philosophy that has already been tested and shown to be effective.
  • "Approved" refers to something officially accepted or authorized, which does not fit the context of describing a philosophy.
  • "Proving" is the present participle, and it doesn’t fit the past tense structure of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "It is a practically proven philosophy."
